title: Why writers delete the key instead of updating it
caption: Two writers that each SET the cache can finish in the opposite order to their database writes, leaving an old value that only the TTL will clear.

messages.label: UPDATE stock = 4
messages.note: Writer 2 commits second, so the database correctly holds 4.

messages.label: SET stock = 5
messages.note: Writer 1 was slow (GC pause, network) and its cache write lands last. The cache now says 5 while the database says 4.

messages.label: fix: DEL stock
messages.note: With delete-on-write both writers just remove the key, and the next read loads 4 from the database.
